question: If the marked price of an article is ₹2,400 and the discount is 16%, then the selling price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price = (100% − Discount%) of Marked Price

SP = (100% − 16%) of ₹2400

SP = 84% × 2400

SP = 84 × 24 = 2016

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2016.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹2,400

Discount = 16%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − (Discount% of MP)

 
 MP = ₹2400 
• − 16% (Discount) SP = ? 
 SP = 2400 − 384 = ₹2016 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount amount = 16% of ₹2,400

⇒ Discount = (16 ÷ 100) × 2400

⇒ Discount = 16 × 24 = ₹384

⇒ SP = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 2400 − 384 = 2016

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2016.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP)

Marked price is the printed price of an article. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.

Direct Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is directly given by: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).
